scope: Read-only integrity review of the two changes in commit 83fcd0236. No source edits, test runs, application captures, or helpers were used.

tablepro_change.source_context: The entire file is under #[cfg(test)] and defines a Harness-based unit test. The removed include_str/assertions read an existing ANSI artifact and checked only that the artifact ends in ESC[?25l and did not contain ESC[?25h.
tablepro_change.removed_assertion_effect: This removes a narrow frozen-fixture integrity assertion about the fixture's cursor-hide terminator. It did not observe the live Harness or application output, so it was not a runtime behavior check and was not production use/replay.
remaining_behavior_assertions: After Ctrl-N, the NAME field owns focus and the empty connection draft is active.
BackTab then Right focuses the test-connection action, clears focus from NAME, and leaves no visible cursor/cursor bar in the Harness state.
Typing into a fresh draft changes it from empty.
tablepro_change.reference_coverage: The same frozen form_advanced scenario remains registered in crates/visual-harness/tests/visual_baseline/scenarios/tablepro.rs and crates/termrock-conformance/tests/visual_baseline/tablepro.rs, with multiple sizes/color profiles. The tracked ANSI artifact remains present at snapshots/tablepro/connections/form_advanced/120x40/truecolor.ansi (HEAD blob a83e2506c1d1d6b732684de993944105fe6be4a5).
tablepro_change.finding: The change removes an irrelevant static-fixture assertion without weakening the live focus/cursor assertions in the unit test or deleting the frozen visual scenario. It does remove a guard that would detect changing this fixture's trailing cursor mode; if that integrity property is required, validate it in the reference-artifact integrity gate or with an actual terminal-mode assertion, rather than coupling it to this unrelated focus unit test.

reach_macro_change.feature_context: reach is behind the default-off testing feature. termrock-shell enables runtime testing only via dev-dependencies/self dev-dependency for its own tests; the reach harness is absent from default production builds.
reach_macro_change.macro_visibility: reach_tests! is #[macro_export] when the testing feature is enabled; it is a testing utility macro, not an ordinary application consumer API.
reach_macro_change.semantics_before: Macro expansion loaded the invoking package's tests/reach_allow.txt into REACH_ALLOW and passed it to reach::check.
reach_macro_change.semantics_after: REACH_ALLOW is the empty string. In gate(), any nonempty missing-word set then differs from the allowed empty set, so every missing word fails; the result is stricter, not more permissive.
reach_macro_change.consumer_inventory: Repository-wide search at current HEAD found no reach_tests! invocation and no tests/reach_allow.txt. The only reach-related unit tests in reach.rs exercise Words parsing/comparison; no test expands the macro or verifies per-consumer allowlist behavior.
reach_macro_change.finding: No current repository consumer or executed case is weakened by this change. However, this silently removes the documented per-size, reasoned-allowlist behavior from an exported testing macro. External consumers with known layout deviations now fail rather than being able to record them; external consumers also no longer need the documented tests/reach_allow.txt. This is a testing-API semantic change and currently has no macro-level test.
reach_macro_change.required_source_resolution: Before treating this as an accepted consumer contract, either (a) retain consumer-configurable allow text/path and add an external/macro-expansion test proving an allowed missing-word case passes and an unlisted one fails, or (b) explicitly make the macro strict-only by updating its docs/API and migration record, and add a consumer compile/test proving this is the intended contract. Do not leave an allowlist-oriented macro silently hardwired to empty while its gate still documents reasoned allow rows.

production_replay_assessment: Neither removed include_str! was used in production screen rendering. TablePro's use was cfg(test) only. Reach's include_str! was emitted by a macro in a default-off test feature. These are not production replay paths. The removed TablePro assertion is a test-fixture check; the reach include is test harness configuration.
recommendation: The TablePro deletion is reasonable as test decoupling, with the narrow fixture-integrity coverage loss recorded. The reach macro change is stricter but changes a documented exported test utility contract; resolve it explicitly or add the missing macro consumer proof. Do not report the reach change as removal of production snapshot replay.
